context.title: The periodic KYC review happens by email, and documents come back for small reasons
context.body: Spendesk's banking partner requires regular KYC reviews. Today the request is emailed from collect@spendesk.com to the Account Owner, who has to gather documents with strict rules: under 3 months old, a signed and dated shareholding structure, IDs in colour front and back, and a personal proof of address for every executive. Validation takes 48 hours or more, and Spendesk's own FAQ lists the usual reasons it stalls: the email went to spam, a document is outdated, a date or signature is missing. Each one costs another round, and the help centre describes no status in between.
assumptions: I haven't used Spendesk's KYC flow myself. My view comes from Spendesk's help-centre KYC articles, public reviews and the job posting, so the product may already do more than I can see.

Automatic checks assume Spendesk can read a document's date, ownership table and signature with document AI, with a person still making the final decision. The prototype shows what the checks would say, not a working model.
Asking a shareholder assumes compliance would accept documents uploaded by the person themselves through a secure link. That needs agreeing with Risk and Compliance.
"Due 12 Dec" and "usually 2 working days" are illustrative. The help centre says validation takes 48 hours or more, and doesn't publish what happens after a deadline.

Built with Grapes, Spendesk's open-source design system (@dev-spendesk/grapes): Callout, Tag, Button, FileCard, Upload, Panel, Timeline, Toast, Avatar, HighlightIcon and its tokens. Grapes' heading font, Roobert, isn't public, so headings use Inter. No Spendesk logo.

goals.title: Right the first time
goals.body: Catch an outdated, unsigned or incomplete document at upload, not 48 hours later.

goals.title: Share the work
goals.body: Let the Account Owner ask shareholders and executives to upload their own documents, without chasing them by email.

goals.title: Never wonder where it stands
goals.body: Show a clear status from request to decision, inside Spendesk.

jtbd: When our bank-required KYC review comes due, I want to know exactly what's needed, get it right the first time and see where the review stands, so our cards and payments keep running without weeks of back and forth.

evidence.step: Reviews are mandatory and come by email
evidence.finding: Spendesk's FAQ says periodic reviews are required by its banking partner. Requests are emailed from collect@spendesk.com to the Account Owner, who handles uploads.

source.label: Spendesk Help: FAQ, our KYC process

evidence.step: The usual blockers are small and preventable
evidence.finding: The same FAQ lists the common problems: the Account Owner didn't get the email, documents are outdated, a date or signature is missing, or an executive is a legal entity.

source.label: Spendesk Help: FAQ, our KYC process

evidence.step: Each round waits 48 hours or more
evidence.finding: Validation takes 48 hours or more depending on the backlog, so every rejected document adds at least another two days.

source.label: Spendesk Help: FAQ, our KYC process

evidence.finding: Only Account Owners can validate the KYC section, and an incomplete shareholding structure will be rejected. The article lists documents but no statuses, deadlines or notifications.

source.label: Spendesk Help: KYC process, Spendesk Financial Services

evidence.finding: The KYC-for-companies article walks through Business Information and Company Structure, then says a human will verify. IDs must be in colour and very clear.

source.label: Spendesk Help: KYC for companies, documents and process

evidence.finding: On Trustpilot (3.8 from 228 reviews), a 2025 review describes waiting 3+ weeks on a verification issue. Spendesk replied that some actions can't happen until identity or device is verified.

approaches: Rewrite the KYC email with a clear checklist and examples
Check each document automatically at upload
Let shareholders and executives upload their own documents
Show a review status and timeline inside Spendesk
Remind the Account Owner in-app, not only by email

ranges.title: Explain the rules better
ranges.summary: Keep the email, but turn it into a clear checklist with the rules and examples for each document.
pros: Fewer documents rejected for misunderstood rules.
cons: Mistakes are still found 48 hours later.

screens.alt: Sketch: KYC email with a checklist of documents and their rules

ranges.title: Check documents at upload
ranges.summary: Every upload is checked straight away for date, ownership and signature, with a specific fix when something is missing.
pros: Catches the FAQ's most common rejections before review.
Uses AI where it clearly helps a person.
cons: The Account Owner still collects everyone's documents.

screens.alt: Sketch: upload screen with pre-checks, one failing for a missing signature

ranges.title: Verification Hub
ranges.summary: One checklist in Spendesk: each item checked at upload, shareholders asked to upload their own documents, and a timeline once it's sent for review.
pros: Covers the three blockers: spam, mistakes, silence.
Spreads the work beyond the Account Owner.
cons: Needs Risk and Compliance to agree on delegated uploads.
More surfaces to build than a better email.

decision.title: Verification Hub: one checklist, checked at upload, shared and tracked
decision.body: Range 3. A checklist inside Spendesk that pre-checks every document, lets the Account Owner ask a shareholder to upload their own ID, and shows the review's status once it's sent.
reasons: The FAQ's blockers are a missed email, a preventable mistake and no status. Only range 3 addresses all three.
Pre-checks turn a 48-hour rejection into a fix in seconds.
Delegation fits how companies work: the Account Owner rarely holds every shareholder's ID.
decision.tradeoff: Automatic checks can be wrong. I'd show them as guidance ("we couldn't find a signature"), let people send anyway with a note, and keep a person making the final decision.

depth.body: Built with Spendesk's open-source Grapes components. Four moments: the checklist shows 4 of 6 items ready with a due date; opening the shareholding structure shows automatic checks, with a missing signature flagged and a way to upload the signed version; asking Thomas, a 32% shareholder, sends him a secure link and tracks it; once everything passes, Send for review unlocks and a timeline shows what happens next. The side panel slides in from the right, the progress bar grows as items turn ready, and motion turns gentler for people who reduce motion. Company, people and documents are fictional.

validation.method: I'd start with KYC rejection reasons and support tickets, then test the hub with Account Owners going through a real periodic review, alongside Risk and Compliance.
hypotheses: Pre-checks reduce documents rejected for date, signature or completeness.
Delegating to shareholders shortens the time from request to submission.
An in-app status reduces "where is my review?" contacts.

metrics.name: First-time pass rate
metrics.definition: Share of reviews approved without any document being sent back.

metrics.name: Time to submit
metrics.definition: Median days from review request to the Account Owner sending everything.

metrics.name: KYC contacts
metrics.definition: Support contacts about KYC reviews per 100 reviews.

nextSteps: Learn how periodic reviews are triggered, assigned and checked today.
Pull rejection reasons and support tickets for the last few review cycles.
Agree with Risk and Compliance which checks can be automated and who may upload.
Test the checklist and pre-checks with Account Owners in English, French and German.
